title: Session proxy degraded during KMS cache invalidation causing dropped audit events in private clusters
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Several private-deployment customers reported missing audit entries and intermittent 5xx errors for control-plane calls during a scheduled KMS key rewrap. Support tickets show a narrow (~30-90s) window where session-proxy requests succeeded functionally but audit ingestion dropped events. Root cause appears to be an interaction between the session-proxy's keyed cache layer and KMS rewrap cache invalidation: on cache invalidation a decryption race caused the proxy to surface soft failures that bypassed the audit write path, effectively dropping audit events for requests served during key refresh.
impact_details: Impacted customers: 3 enterprise Private customers reported missing audit records (SUP-20234, SUP-20258, SUP-20311). Symptom window: 2025-02-11T03:12:00Z -> ~2025-02-11T03:13:45Z. Side effects: control-plane calls returned 200 but downstream auditing pipeline showed gaps; some downstream operators saw 502 errors when decrypt-and-forward code retried. Severity: P0 due to audit/logging loss for regulated workloads.
how_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy private control-plane with KMS key TTL configured low (e.g., 60s) and enable session-proxy keyed caching. 2) Trigger key rewrap (simulate timeline when KMS re-encrypts envelopes). 3) Flood ~500 concurrent control-plane requests while invalidation occurs. 4) Observe decryption failures in session-proxy logs, followed by audit write skips. Links to repro harness: https://internal.redwood.com/ci/repro/ENG-564738
root_cause_analysis: The session-proxy holds a lightweight cache of tenant keystore handles to avoid sync KMS calls on every request. When an external rewrap event invalidates the cache, concurrent requests race: request A notices cache miss and issues an async refresh; request B attempts decrypt with the stale handle and sees a decryption error. The decrypt error follows a non-fatal code path that marks the request as served (response to caller) but does not enqueue the audit event because the audit write assumes decryption success. Additionally, KMS client retries caused transient envelope-ID mismatches that surfaced as 'decrypt: key-not-current' errors. In short: race between cache invalidation + async refresh and audit write dependency on successful decrypt leads to silent audit drops.
short_term_mitigation: 1) Roll back recent change that reduced session-proxy cache TTL for affected clusters (rollback performed 2025-02-12 08:00Z). 2) Patch control plane to treat decryption failure as retriable synchronous path that will fetch a fresh key before considering request completed. 3) Add a temporary audit-queue buffer to persist audit events on decrypt-path failures until decryption or explicit drop decision resolves. Hotfix branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/10987
long_term_fix_plan: - Change session-proxy cache semantics: on cache miss, perform synchronous fetch-with-backoff for the first N concurrent requests rather than async refresh. - Ensure audit path is decoupled from transient decryption failures: buffer audit events for up to 120s and mark for guaranteed retry with at-least-once semantics. - Add explicit metrics/alerts for 'audit_buffered', 'audit_dropped', and 'kms_decrypt_retries' and a dashboard. - Backport fix to runtime-1.20 and runtime-1.19 maintenance branches for customers on older stacks.
test_and_validation: Unit tests: new mocks for KMS envelope TTL + cache race. Integration: staging run that replays repro harness with high concurrency; assertion that audit ingestion equals request count. E2E: deploy to 'canary-private-1' (10% of private clusters) overnight and validate dashboards for 48 hours. Automated post-deploy checks: verify no audit gaps for 24h and KMS error rate fall below 0.1%.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge hotfix to main and build canary image. 2) Canary to canary-private-1 (10% traffic) for 6h verify. 3) Expand to remaining private clusters in waves over 8 hours. 4) Notify Dedicated customers with identical runtime to schedule maintenance window for backport. Rollback: revert to previous image (fast) and re-enable previous cache TTL.
monitoring_and_alerts: New alerts: KMS.decrypt_rate_spike > 0.5% sustained 5m, audit_buffered > 1000 events, audit_dropped > 10 in 1m. Dashboards: private-controlplane/kms-decrypt, private-controlplane/audit-pipeline, private-controlplane/session-proxy-cache. Link: https://dashboards.redwood.com/d/pcp-kms-audit
